hero.headline: Trump to nominate Todd Blanche as attorney general
hero.body:
President Trump announced at a White House dinner that he will nominate Todd Blanche to serve as attorney general. A video of the event was posted on social media by a White House aide, capturing Trump's statement that he plans to formally nominate Blanche.

Blanche, who has served as one of Trump's personal attorneys, would lead the Department of Justice if confirmed by the Senate. The attorney general oversees federal law enforcement, including the FBI, and directs the department's legal positions on behalf of the executive branch. The role has remained one of the most politically sensitive positions in the cabinet.

The announcement comes as Trump continues to shape his administration with loyalists in key positions. Blanche represented Trump in several high-profile legal matters before the president returned to office. His nomination will require Senate confirmation, where Republicans hold a majority but must still navigate the confirmation process.

The choice of Blanche signals Trump's continued preference for advisers with whom he has personal relationships and trust. The attorney general position has seen significant turnover during Trump's political career, with past occupants facing pressure over the independence of the Justice Department versus loyalty to the president.

However, Blanche faces immediate scrutiny over his handling of the Epstein Files Transparency Act. An investigative journalist and legal analyst filed a lawsuit in Washington DC federal court accusing Blanche of a "brazen, shocking, and ongoing violation" of the law requiring the Justice Department to release all documents related to Jeffrey Epstein. Congress passed the transparency act in November with a December 19, 2025 deadline for full document release.

The lawsuit alleges that Blanche, who served as deputy attorney general, has delayed the process and released only a fraction of available documents. It accuses him of missing statutory deadlines for document production, making improper redactions, failing to explain redactions as required by law, and withholding documents after release.

Blanche has argued that redactions were necessary to protect the identities of Epstein's victims, many of them minors, and acknowledged that "mistakes are inevitable." However, critics have questioned the department's process for determining which papers to withhold and which redactions to make. Some victims have complained that their sensitive personal information was improperly exposed in releases.

The Justice Department's office of the inspector general launched an audit into the department's compliance with the Epstein Files Transparency Act last week.

If confirmed, Blanche would take over the Justice Department at a time when it faces questions about prosecutorial priorities and its relationship with the White House. The formal nomination is expected to be submitted to the Senate in the coming days, beginning what could be a contentious confirmation battle where his record on transparency and document release will likely come under intense examination.

cards.headline: Israel and Lebanon agree to full ceasefire contingent on Hezbollah withdrawal
cards.teaser: Israel and Lebanon reached a ceasefire agreement that requires Hezbollah to halt attacks and withdraw operatives from southern Lebanon.
cards.body:
Israel and Lebanon have agreed to implement a full ceasefire to end hostilities, according to a joint statement from the US State Department. The agreement requires Hezbollah to completely halt attacks and withdraw all operatives from southern Lebanon.

The US rejected "any attempt, by any state or non-state actor, to hold Lebanon's future hostage." The ceasefire represents a significant development as the Trump administration seeks to overcome barriers to a broader agreement with Iran, of which Hezbollah is aligned.

cards.headline: Iran attacks Kuwait airport, killing one and injuring dozens
cards.body:
Iranian drones struck Kuwait's international airport, killing at least one person and wounding 63 others. The attack damaged a passenger terminal and forced the airport to suspend traffic and redirect incoming flights to alternative airports.

The strike represents a significant escalation in the Gulf region and marks the first deadly attack since a ceasefire took effect on April 8. Iran said the assault was retaliation for earlier US military action, including a strike on an Iranian oil tanker near the Strait of Hormuz and attacks on Iran's Qeshm Island.

The sequence of events began when US Central Command targeted an unladen tanker, the M/T Lexie, in international waters as it moved toward Iran's Kharg Island near Kuwait. US forces fired a Hellfire missile to disable the vessel's engine after the crew ignored repeated warnings over 24 hours. In response, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps attacked the US Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain with missiles and drones, a claim the US military denied. The Iranian military also launched three attack drones toward civilian ships in regional waters, which US forces said they shot down.

Kuwait's defense ministry called the airport attack "criminal Iranian aggression" causing significant material damage. The country summoned Iran's diplomatic representative to formally protest and ordered a reduction in Iranian embassy staff. Kuwait declared two Iranian diplomats persona non grata and gave them 24 hours to leave.

Iran's foreign ministry blamed Kuwait and Bahrain for the attacks, condemning what it described as the "colonialist use" of their territory and infrastructure by the United States to advance military plans against Iran. The statement held Kuwait and Bahrain's leaders "directly and unmistakably responsible" for the earlier strikes.

The attacks undermine ongoing diplomatic efforts between the United States and Iran. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio claimed during congressional testimony that a nuclear deal could be imminent, suggesting progress on aspects of Iran's nuclear program previously off limits for negotiation. However, Iran has indicated it would suspend peace talks in protest of the US actions.

Donald Trump said he is not seeking to escalate tensions and that talks with Iran continue. He claimed Iran is "pretty close" to signing a peace agreement and suggested it "could happen over the weekend." Trump also expressed interest in meeting Iran's supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned that Iran is "playing with fire" and suggested Trump could order a "full-scale return to military action" if negotiations fail. Netanyahu asserted that Israel and US forces remain ready for military operations.

The latest exchange of strikes highlights the fragility of ceasefire arrangements and the difficulty of achieving diplomatic breakthroughs amid continued military confrontation in the Middle East.

cards.headline: Trump removes job protections from 8,000 senior federal employees
cards.teaser: An executive order moved thousands of federal positions to a new classification that removes civil service protections.
cards.body:
President Trump signed an executive order removing job protections from roughly 8,000 senior federal employees earning up to about $200,000 annually. These workers, deemed to be "influencing" government policy, were reclassified into a new employment category that allows them to be fired without cause.

The order strips away civil service protections that have traditionally shielded career government employees from political dismissals. The move is part of the administration's broader effort to overhaul the federal workforce.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Shifts Legal Strategy to Justify Tariffs
cards.teaser: The administration is using forced labor laws as a basis for imposing trade restrictions.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has adopted forced labor laws as its legal rationale for maintaining tariffs, viewing this approach as more legally and politically sustainable than previous justifications. The shift in strategy aims to defend existing trade restrictions against legal challenges and international pressure.

Critics contend that emphasizing forced labor concerns masks protectionist motives rather than reflecting genuine commitment to labor practices. The administration continues to pursue new tariffs as well, including a proposed 25% levy on Brazilian imports based on claims of unreasonable trade practices.

cards.headline: Ukrainian drones strike St. Petersburg during economic forum
cards.teaser: The attacks hit an oil refinery and other targets in Russia's second-largest city on the opening day of an international economic showcase.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drones targeted oil storage facilities near St. Petersburg as Russia's annual economic forum opened in the city. The attacks set fire to an oil terminal, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The strikes occurred ahead of Vladimir Putin's scheduled address at the event, which is often referred to as Russia's answer to the World Economic Forum in Davos.

The drone attacks demonstrate Ukraine's capacity to reach targets deep inside Russian territory, striking major urban centers far from active fighting. The timing coincided with Russia's showcase economic event, one of Putin's flagship annual gatherings.

cards.headline: Taiwan president calls on China to acknowledge Tiananmen crackdown
cards.teaser: The remarks came as China prevented activists from marking the anniversary and banned the Tiananmen Mothers group from visiting a cemetery.
cards.body:
Taiwan's president called on China to acknowledge the truth about the Tiananmen Square crackdown. The statement came as Chinese authorities escalated efforts to suppress commemoration of the event, with police in Hong Kong quickly stopping an artist attempting to mark the anniversary. Amnesty International described China's ban on the Tiananmen Mothers visiting a cemetery as heartless and a signal of escalating repression.

Activists said they continue to receive new photographs each year documenting the crackdown, reflecting ongoing efforts to preserve the memory despite government pressure. China has maintained strict controls on discussion of the events and increased restrictions on public commemoration in recent years.

cards.headline: Israel and Lebanon renew ceasefire agreement
cards.teaser: The US-brokered deal calls for a complete cessation of fire from Hezbollah and the evacuation of militia operatives from southern Lebanon.
cards.body:
Israel and Lebanon have agreed to implement a ceasefire aimed at ending hostilities in the region. The US-brokered agreement requires Hezbollah, an Iranian-backed militia operating in southern Lebanon, to completely stop attacks and withdraw its operatives from the country's south.

The Trump administration announced the deal as part of broader efforts to overcome barriers to negotiations between the United States and Iran. Both countries rejected attempts by state or non-state actors to control Lebanon's future. A previous ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon had largely been ignored.

cards.headline: Ukrainian drones strike St. Petersburg during economic forum

cards.headline: Germany loses UN Security Council seat bid
cards.teaser: Germany blamed Russia for its defeat in the election, saying Moscow stirred up sentiment against Berlin over its support for Ukraine.
cards.body:
Germany failed to secure a seat on the UN Security Council in what officials described as a bitter defeat. Five countries were elected to the council instead, including Kyrgyzstan, which won a seat for the first time.

German lawmaker Johann Wadephul said Russia had actively worked against Germany's bid, stirring up opposition due to Germany's support for Ukraine. The loss represents a significant diplomatic setback for the German government.

cards.headline: Taiwan president calls on China to acknowledge Tiananmen crackdown
cards.teaser: The remarks came as China prevented activists from marking the anniversary and banned the Tiananmen Mothers group from visiting a cemetery.
cards.body:

cards.headline: China bans four New Zealand lawmakers over Taiwan visit
cards.teaser: The lawmakers were informed of a one-year ban from China after returning from Taiwan last month.
cards.body:
China has imposed a one-year ban on four New Zealand members of parliament following their visit to Taiwan last month. The lawmakers learned of the restriction upon returning home.

China views Taiwan as part of its territory and regularly protests when foreign politicians visit the island. The ban demonstrates Beijing's approach to discouraging countries from engaging with Taiwan diplomatically.

cards.headline: Iran's soccer chief seeks US visas for World Cup team
cards.teaser: The head of Iran's football federation said he has been working with FIFA to obtain visas as the tournament begins next week.
cards.body:
Mehdi Taj, head of Iran's football federation, said his organization is working with FIFA to secure visas for Iran's national team to compete in the World Cup, which begins next week. Rather than dealing directly with the United States, Taj indicated the federation expects FIFA to help facilitate the team's participation.

The visa challenge reflects broader tensions between the countries. Iran faces international isolation over its military actions and nuclear program, and the World Cup's hosting in the United States creates diplomatic obstacles for Iranian athletes seeking entry.

hero.headline: Trump removes job protections from 8,000 senior federal employees
hero.teaser: An executive order moved thousands of federal positions to a new classification that removes civil service protections.
hero.body:
President Trump signed an executive order removing job protections from roughly 8,000 senior federal employees earning up to about $200,000 annually. These workers, deemed to be "influencing" government policy, were reclassified into a new employment category that allows them to be fired without cause.

The order strips away civil service protections that have traditionally shielded career government employees from political dismissals. The move is part of the administration's broader effort to overhaul the federal workforce.

cards.headline: Trump to nominate Todd Blanche as attorney general
cards.teaser: The president announced plans to make his current attorney general's appointment permanent.
cards.body:
President Trump said he will nominate Todd Blanche to serve as attorney general on a permanent basis. Trump called Blanche a very talented individual when announcing his intention to formalize the appointment. Blanche has been serving in the role and previously stated that anti-weaponization fund proposals are no longer being pursued.

Blanche also indicated that Trump remains protected from certain tax enforcement actions under current policy. The nomination will require Senate confirmation. Blanche's transition from acting to permanent status comes as the administration continues to reshape the Justice Department.

cards.headline: Flesh-eating screwworm detected in Texas livestock
cards.teaser: Federal agriculture officials confirmed the first case of the parasite in the United States after it crossed from Mexico.
cards.body:
The U.S. Department of Agriculture confirmed that New World screwworm was detected in a Texas calf, marking the parasite's arrival in the United States. The flesh-eating pest crossed the border from Mexico and poses a significant threat to livestock and food production. The USDA has updated its status monitoring for the parasite.

Screwworm larvae feed on living tissue of warm-blooded animals and can cause severe damage or death if untreated. The detection triggered federal and state agricultural response protocols. Officials are working to prevent the parasite's spread beyond the initial case in Texas livestock.

cards.headline: Ohio State settles sexual abuse claims for $100 million
cards.teaser: The university reached an agreement with nearly 300 survivors who said they were abused by a former team doctor.
cards.body:
Ohio State University agreed to a $100 million settlement with approximately 300 former students who alleged sexual abuse by Richard Strauss, a doctor who worked at the university for decades. The settlement resolves the remaining civil litigation related to the abuse claims.

The accusers said they were abused during medical examinations conducted by Strauss. Ohio State had previously settled claims with other groups of accusers in related cases stemming from the same allegations.

cards.headline: Israel and Lebanon agree to ceasefire contingent on Hezbollah actions
cards.teaser: The United States brokered an agreement between the two countries to renew their ceasefire arrangement.
cards.body:
Israel and Lebanon have agreed to implement a ceasefire to end hostilities, according to an announcement by the Trump administration. The agreement requires Iran-aligned Hezbollah to completely cease fire and evacuate all its operatives from southern Lebanon. The US State Department said both countries reject "any attempt, by any state or non-state actor, to hold Lebanon's future hostage."

The ceasefire represents part of the Trump administration's broader efforts to address regional tensions and overcome barriers to reaching a deal with Iran. US diplomats negotiated the framework between Israel and Lebanon in Washington.

cards.headline: Jury awards $176 million in wrongful death case over crash that killed two boys
cards.teaser: Rebecca Grossman and former Dodgers player Scott Erickson were found negligent in the deaths.
cards.body:
A jury awarded $176 million to the Iskander family in a civil case stemming from a fatal crash that killed two brothers. Rebecca Grossman, a socialite, and Scott Erickson, a former Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher, were found liable for the deaths. The family had originally sought $439 million in damages.

The jury's verdict determined that both defendants were negligent in the collision. Grossman had previously faced criminal proceedings related to the same incident.

cards.headline: SpaceX sets valuation at $1.75 trillion ahead of stock market debut
cards.teaser: The space exploration company established a target

hero.headline: SpaceX Sets $1.77 Trillion Valuation Ahead of Record-Breaking IPO
hero.body:
SpaceX has acquired Elon Musk's artificial intelligence company xAI in a major merger that consolidates parts of his business empire as the aerospace company prepares for a public listing. The deal, announced Monday on SpaceX's website, values SpaceX at $1 trillion and xAI at $250 billion, setting the combined entity on course for a stock market valuation exceeding $1 trillion.

The merger creates what the companies described as "the most ambitious, vertically-integrated innovation engine on (and off) Earth, with AI, rockets, space-based internet, direct-to-mobile device communications and the world's foremost real-time information and free speech platform." Through the acquisition, SpaceX gains xAI's Grok chatbot and the social media platform X.

The consolidation reflects Musk's strategy to combine space technology with artificial intelligence infrastructure. Both companies cited plans for space-based datacenters powered by solar-powered satellites as central to the merger's rationale. According to the announcement, current AI advances depend on large terrestrial datacenters that consume enormous amounts of power and cooling. The companies stated that "global electricity demand for AI simply cannot be met with terrestrial solutions, even in the near term, without imposing hardship on communities and the environment" and that "in the long term, space-based AI is obviously the only way to scale."

The IPO is expected to occur in early summer, timed to coincide with a planetary alignment and Musk's birthday on June 28. Musk confirmed the deal minimally on X, responding with "yes" to posts referencing merger reports.

Both companies have experienced significant valuation growth recently. SpaceX revealed an expected value of $800 billion in a December letter to investors as it continues dominating satellite launches and securing contracts with the U.S. federal government. xAI raised $20 billion in a Series E funding round last month that valued the company at $230 billion, despite controversy surrounding its Grok chatbot over promotion of racist content and nonconsensual deepfake images.

The merger comes as Musk has increasingly intertwined his various business interests. xAI acquired the platform X in an all-stock transaction in early 2025, and Tesla announced plans last month to invest $2 billion in xAI.

The announcement provides Musk with positive momentum after Tesla released disappointing earnings showing declining revenues and a struggling car business. The news also comes days after the Department of Justice released files related to Jeffrey Epstein that showed Musk exchanging friendly emails with the disgraced financier. Musk called the email release a "distraction" and stated he was "well aware that some email correspondence with him could be misinterpreted and used by detractors to smear my name."

cards.headline: New World Screwworm Found in U.S. Cattle for First Time Since 1960s
cards.teaser: The Agriculture Department confirmed a case of the flesh-eating pest in a Texas calf.
cards.body:
The Agriculture Department confirmed the presence of New World screwworm in a calf in South Texas, marking the first case detected in the United States since the 1960s. The flesh-eating parasite poses a serious threat to livestock and represents a significant development for the agricultural industry.

The screwworm was eradicated from the U.S. decades ago through a coordinated pest management program. The reappearance of the parasite in domestic cattle raises concerns about biosecurity and the potential for further infestations affecting livestock operations across the country.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Fall as Middle East Tensions Escalate
cards.teaser: The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped more than 600 points following renewed clashes.
cards.body:
U.S. stock markets declined as investors responded to escalating Middle East tensions. The Dow fell more than 600 points, ending the S&P 500's nine-day winning streak. Oil prices climbed back toward $100 per barrel amid heightened geopolitical concerns.

The selloff extended to Asia-Pacific markets, which opened lower as Middle East fighting intensified. The sharp reversal halted Wall Street's recent rally as investors reassessed their positions in light of the regional conflict.

cards.headline: Pace Gallery Cuts 50 Artists and 50 Staff Amid Art Market Downturn
cards.teaser: The established gallery is contracting in response to challenging market conditions.
cards.body:
Pace Gallery announced it is dropping 50 artists from its roster and eliminating 50 staff positions as the art market faces significant headwinds. The cuts represent a substantial contraction for one of the art world's most established players.

The reductions reflect broader difficulties in the contemporary art market, which has seen declining sales and reduced buyer activity. Even prominent galleries with decades of history are being forced to reduce their operations in response to the challenging economic environment for art sales.

cards.teaser: The administration is using forced labor laws as a basis for imposing trade restrictions.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has adopted forced labor laws as its legal rationale for maintaining tariffs, viewing this approach as more legally and politically sustainable than previous justifications. The shift in strategy aims to defend existing trade restrictions against legal challenges and international pressure.

Critics contend that emphasizing forced labor concerns masks protectionist motives rather than reflecting genuine commitment to labor practices. The administration continues to pursue new tariffs as well, including a proposed 25% levy on Brazilian imports based on claims of unreasonable trade practices.

cards.headline: Colorado Governor Vetoes Bills on Credit Card Fees and Firefighter Cancer Benefits
cards.teaser: Governor Jared Polis set a personal record for vetoes in rejecting multiple pieces of legislation.
cards.body:
Governor Jared Polis vetoed legislation that would have limited credit card swipe fees and provided additional benefits to firefighters diagnosed with cancer, setting a personal veto record.

According to reporting, Polis also rejected a bill banning surveillance pricing—a practice where companies use data to set different prices for workers' wages and consumer goods. Colorado's proposed measure would have been the nation's strongest protection against algorithmic pricing, more expansive than Maryland's April approval of a grocery store surveillance pricing ban. Consumer advocates criticized the veto, saying the governor sided with corporations over workers.

cards.headline: Lab-Grown Diamonds Increase Pressure on Natural Diamond Miners
cards.teaser: The synthetic diamond industry's growth is creating challenges for traditional miners.
cards.body:
The rising popularity of lab-grown diamonds is putting significant pressure on companies and individuals who search for natural gemstones. The synthetic diamond market has expanded rapidly as technology has improved and prices have fallen.

Traditional diamond miners face increased competition from laboratory-produced stones that are chemically identical to natural diamonds but cost substantially less. One miner described the search for natural diamonds as dependent on divine fortune, highlighting the uncertainty facing an industry confronting new technological competition.

hero.headline: NASA ends Mars MAVEN mission after orbital failure
hero.body:
NASA has confirmed the end of its Mars Atmosphere and Volatile Evolution mission after losing contact with the spacecraft. The orbiter stopped communicating with ground stations over the weekend after operating normally before passing behind Mars. When it reappeared from behind the planet, the spacecraft remained silent.

"Telemetry showed all subsystems working normally before it orbited behind Mars," NASA said in a statement. The spacecraft and operations teams investigated the anomaly, but ground controllers were unable to restore contact or functionality. NASA declared MAVEN in an unrecoverable state after attempting to reestablish communications for six months.

MAVEN launched in 2013 and reached Mars the following year to begin its mission studying the upper Martian atmosphere and its interaction with the solar wind. During its more than a decade in orbit, the spacecraft collected extensive data about how Mars loses atmospheric gases to space. Scientists used MAVEN's findings to understand a fundamental question about the planet's history.

The research helped explain how Mars transformed from a world that may have been wet and warm to the cold and dry environment observed today. The sun itself played a crucial role in this transformation. Solar wind and radiation drove processes that stripped away most of the planet's atmosphere over billions of years, fundamentally changing Mars' climate and surface conditions.

Beyond its primary scientific mission, MAVEN served an important operational function. The spacecraft acted as a communications relay for NASA's two Mars rovers, Curiosity and Perseverance. These rovers have conducted extensive exploration of the planet and made numerous scientific discoveries that depend partly on MAVEN's relay capabilities.

The loss of MAVEN reduces NASA's fleet of active Mars orbiters but does not leave the agency without atmospheric monitoring capabilities. Two other NASA spacecraft continue to operate around Mars. Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, launched in 2005, and Mars Odyssey, launched in 2001, remain active and continue studying the planet and supporting ongoing surface missions.

The mission significantly exceeded its original planned lifespan, continuing to transmit valuable scientific data well beyond initial expectations. MAVEN completed thousands of orbits around Mars during its operational period and made key discoveries about atmospheric escape processes.

Most NASA spacecraft missions at Mars end through planned decommissioning rather than sudden anomalies. The unexpected loss of MAVEN after so many years of successful operation marked an unusual conclusion to the long-running mission. Despite the loss, NASA continues to develop future Mars exploration missions as part of its broader planetary science program, maintaining its commitment to understanding the red planet and supporting ongoing surface exploration efforts.

cards.headline: Flesh-eating screwworm detected in South Texas
cards.teaser: The USDA confirmed the first detection of the parasitic fly across the US-Mexico border.
cards.body:
The US Department of Agriculture confirmed a flesh-eating screwworm infection in South Texas, marking the fly's first breach of the US-Mexico border. The detection represents a significant agricultural and public health concern as the parasite can infest livestock and other warm-blooded animals.

Screwworms lay eggs in open wounds, and the hatched larvae feed on living tissue. The United States eradicated the pest domestically decades ago through sustained control programs, but the fly remains present in parts of Central and South America.

cards.headline: Meteor that landed off Cape Cod identified as iron
cards.teaser: NASA analyzed a meteor that exploded over Massachusetts with the force of 300 tons of TNT.
cards.body:
NASA determined that a meteor which landed off Cape Cod was made of iron. The space rock, approximately three feet across, entered the atmosphere over New England traveling at 75,000 mph and broke apart with energy equivalent to roughly 300 tons of TNT. The explosion occurred over Massachusetts and generated a boom heard from Delaware to Montreal.

The atmospheric breakup scattered fragments across a wide area, with some pieces falling into waters off Cape Cod. The sound traveled farther than any of the meteor's fragments, reaching across much of the northeastern United States and into Canada.

cards.headline: Northern lights may be visible across eight states
cards.teaser: A geomagnetic storm watch was issued for multiple nights this week.
cards.body:
Forecasters predict the northern lights could be visible across eight states as a G3 geomagnetic storm watch was issued. The aurora borealis may appear over parts of the northern United States, with viewing opportunities expected through multiple nights this week.

The geomagnetic storm conditions result from solar activity that sends charged particles toward Earth. When these particles interact with the planet's magnetic field and atmosphere, they create the colorful light displays typically visible only at high latitudes. Strong storms can push the viewing zone farther south than usual.

cards.headline: Apple plans to use Nvidia chips for Gemini-powered Siri
cards.teaser: The company is preparing AI infrastructure ahead of its June 8 developer conference.
cards.body:
Apple plans to use Nvidia chips to power a new version of Siri running on Google's Gemini technology, according to a new report. The development comes as Apple prepares for its Worldwide Developers Conference on June 8, where the company is expected to unveil its latest AI strategy.

The integration represents a shift in Apple's approach to artificial intelligence and voice assistant technology. Apple has faced pressure to modernize Siri as competitors release more capable AI assistants. The company's upcoming iOS 27 release is expected to include new features tied to these AI improvements.

cards.headline: Benchmark raises $2 billion, launches first growth fund
cards.teaser: The venture capital firm abandoned its longtime practice of limiting fund sizes to $425 million.
cards.body:
Benchmark raised $2 billion in new capital and launched its first growth fund, breaking with a tradition of more than 20 years. The firm had previously maintained a practice of keeping its funds at approximately $425 million, distinguishing itself from competitors who raised increasingly large pools of capital.

The capital raise and new growth fund structure mark a strategic shift for one of Silicon Valley's most prominent venture firms. Benchmark has backed companies including Uber, Twitter, and Snapchat using its previous fund model. The larger fund size will allow the firm to make bigger investments and follow companies through later funding stages.

cards.headline: Samsung announces AI health features for Galaxy Watch
cards.teaser: The company introduced new capabilities for its wearable devices.
cards.body:
Samsung introduced new AI-powered health features for its Galaxy Watch line, positioning the devices as everyday health companions. The announcement included details about next-generation capabilities designed to provide users with more comprehensive health monitoring and insights.

The enhanced features build on Samsung's existing health tracking technology, adding artificial intelligence to analyze user data and provide personalized recommendations. The company continues to compete with Apple and other manufacturers in the smartwatch and health wearables market.

hero.headline: Russell Wilson retires from NFL after 14 seasons, joins CBS as broadcaster
hero.body:
Russell Wilson has announced his retirement from professional football, ending a 14-season career in the National Football League. The quarterback has confirmed that he will transition into a broadcasting role with CBS.

During his time in the NFL, Wilson established himself as a prominent quarterback. His career included a Super Bowl championship and multiple playoff appearances, primarily during his years with the Seattle Seahawks before he played for other franchises. The announcement concludes a significant chapter in professional football.

The later stages of Wilson's career drew considerable attention as his performance declined from his earlier years. This trajectory has influenced how analysts and fans evaluate his overall legacy. Some have questioned whether his earlier accomplishments will be enough to support a Hall of Fame candidacy, given the contrast with his final seasons in the league.

Wilson's transition to CBS follows a common path for retired NFL players moving into sports media. The network has not released specific details about his broadcasting responsibilities or which programs will feature his contributions. His extensive experience as a veteran quarterback is expected to inform his analysis and commentary on the sport.

The Detroit Lions, led by head coach Aaron Glenn, acknowledged Wilson's retirement and his new position. Glenn noted that the team is in the process of evaluating quarterback options as they prepare for the upcoming season. With Wilson's departure from active play, teams seeking experienced signal-callers will have one fewer veteran option available in the market.

Wilson's career represents a significant presence in modern NFL history. He led the Seahawks during a period of competitive excellence and was part of one of the league's most recognizable rosters. His time with the team produced memorable moments and established him as a fixture in professional football.

The move to broadcasting represents a natural progression for a player with Wilson's experience level. Former players often bring valuable perspective to sports media through their playing backgrounds. Wilson's years at the quarterback position, combined with his playoff and championship experience, position him to provide informed analysis of current NFL play.

The timing of Wilson's announcement comes as the NFL offseason continues and teams finalize their roster decisions. His retirement removes another notable name from the pool of available veteran players. For CBS, adding a quarterback with his level of experience and profile strengthens their broadcasting team.

Wilson's decision to enter broadcasting rather than pursue other opportunities reflects the increasing trend of prominent athletes leveraging their professional experience in media roles. His next chapter represents a shift from on-field competition to analysis and commentary, allowing him to remain connected to the sport while transitioning away from active play.

cards.headline: Jalen Brunson leads Knicks to Game 1 victory over Spurs in NBA Finals
cards.teaser: The New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs in the opening game of the NBA Finals behind a strong performance from guard Jalen Brunson.
cards.body:
Jalen Brunson scored 30 points to lead the New York Knicks to a 105-95 victory over the San Antonio Spurs in Game 1 of the NBA Finals. Playing on the Spurs' home court, the Knicks kept Victor Wembanyama quiet for stretches of the game while maintaining their momentum from an 11-game winning streak in the playoffs.

The victory puts the Knicks just three wins away from their first championship since 1973. The Spurs, who defeated the defending champion Oklahoma City Thunder in the previous round, were unable to contain Brunson's offensive performance in the opening contest of the series.

cards.headline: Aaron Judge awaits diagnosis as Yankees conduct additional injury testing
cards.teaser: The New York Yankees are waiting for results of further tests on outfielder Aaron Judge's rib cage injury.
cards.body:
Aaron Judge will undergo additional medical testing as the Yankees work to determine the severity of his rib cage injury. The team is awaiting test results that will clarify his timeline for return to action.

Judge's injury status is a major concern for the Yankees' lineup and season plans. The slugger's health will play a key role in the team's performance in the coming weeks.

cards.headline: NBA Commissioner Adam Silver discusses expansion plans ahead of Finals
cards.teaser: Commissioner Adam Silver confirmed that NBA expansion discussions are ongoing, with interest from ownership groups in Las Vegas and Seattle.
cards.body:
Adam Silver confirmed that expansion discussions are ongoing, with the NBA considering adding new franchises to Las Vegas and Seattle. Multiple ownership groups have expressed interest in bringing teams to these markets, indicating active momentum behind the league's expansion efforts.

Silver addressed several other league matters during his media availability before the Finals, including competitive balance and tanking concerns. The commissioner expressed satisfaction with the league's current direction on multiple fronts.

cards.headline: Jon Cooper wins Jack Adams Award as NHL coach of the year
cards.teaser: Tampa Bay Lightning coach Jon Cooper received the Jack Adams Award after his 14th season with the franchise.
cards.body:
Jon Cooper was named the NHL's coach of the year, earning the Jack Adams Award for his work with the Tampa Bay Lightning. Cooper, who has coached the team for 14 seasons, stated he never expected to win the honor. The award recognizes the league's top coach as voted by the Professional Hockey Writers' Association.

Lindy Ruff of another franchise was also a finalist for the award but did not win. Cooper's recognition comes after guiding the Lightning through another successful season. The award adds to Cooper's extensive list of accomplishments with Tampa Bay, where he has built one of the league's most consistent programs.

cards.headline: Padres release Nick Castellanos after 39-game stint
cards.teaser: The San Diego Padres designated outfielder Nick Castellanos for assignment following a difficult stretch with the team.
cards.body:
The San Diego Padres designated Nick Castellanos for assignment after just 39 games with the team. The move comes following a disappointing stretch that failed to address the club's offensive issues.

Castellanos, a former All-Star, did not perform as expected during his brief tenure in San Diego. The decision to part ways represents a shift in the team's roster composition rather than a comprehensive solution to their offensive struggles.

cards.headline: Ukraine-Russia conflict casts shadow over French Open semifinals
cards.teaser: The ongoing war in Ukraine will provide an unavoidable backdrop to the French Open women's semifinals and potentially the final.
cards.body:
Russia's war in Ukraine will form an inescapable backdrop to the French Open women's semi-finals and potentially the final, depending on which players advance through the tournament.

Tennis authorities have faced difficult decisions regarding the participation of Russian and Belarusian players at international competitions since the conflict began, implementing varying policies across different sporting events worldwide.

hero.headline: Martin Scorsese Joins AI Company as Advisor, Drawing Backlash from Filmmakers
hero.body:
Martin Scorsese has been appointed as a partner and adviser to Black Forest Labs, a German-based artificial intelligence company specializing in text-to-image generative technology. The New York Times reported the arrangement began in 2025, and Scorsese has stated he uses the AI tools to create storyboards for his filmmaking work.

The announcement has sparked sharp criticism from fellow filmmakers and creative professionals who view the partnership as a betrayal of working artists. Boots Riley, director of "Sorry to Bother You," responded bluntly to the news, suggesting Scorsese received substantial compensation for the role. "Boots Riley came out swinging," according to Deadline, guessing that Scorsese joined the firm as an adviser "to help provide for his family and that Scorsese doesn't give a fuck since he thinks AI will fall on its face anyway."

The backlash reflects growing tension in the entertainment industry over artificial intelligence's role in creative work. The Guardian reported that artists feel betrayed by Scorsese's endorsement, accusing him of throwing them under the bus by lending his considerable credibility to AI development in filmmaking.

Scorsese has defended his involvement with the technology, describing it as "creatively freeing." He has emphasized that the immediacy of communicating his vision to cast and crew through AI-generated storyboards enhances his creative process. The BBC noted that his endorsement carries significant weight given his legendary status in cinema and his long history of advocating for film preservation and traditional filmmaking methods.

The controversy highlights deeper concerns within the entertainment industry about job displacement. Writers, actors, and visual artists have expressed worry that AI tools could replace human creative labor. Artist and writer Jess Harwood published an opinion piece in The Guardian arguing that AI art is "boring, soulless theft" that kills the planet through energy-intensive data centers. She wrote that as a visual artist seeing AI-generated images presented as art, "I see red."

The divide over AI adoption continues to widen as prominent figures take opposing positions. Kane Parsons, the 20-year-old director behind the Backrooms series, recently told The Australian that using AI defeats the purpose of filmmaking and that he gets no enjoyment from such tools.

Black Forest Labs specializes in generative AI technology capable of creating images and visual content from text descriptions. The company has attracted significant interest in the venture capital world, with AI investments and valuations reaching unprecedented levels across the technology sector.

Scorsese's partnership marks one of the most high-profile endorsements of AI in creative industries, making the backlash particularly notable given his stature and his previous advocacy for traditional filmmaking approaches.

cards.headline: Questlove Documentary on Earth, Wind & Fire Opens Tribeca Festival
cards.teaser: The festival opened with a documentary portrait of the band directed by Questlove.
cards.body:
Questlove's documentary about Earth, Wind & Fire premiered at the opening of the Tribeca Festival on Wednesday. The film tells the story of the legendary band and Maurice White, presenting them as significantly underrated figures in pop music.

Robert De Niro, the festival's co-founder, used his opening remarks to criticize Donald Trump, describing him as immoral, cruel and corrupt. De Niro established the festival following the September 11 attacks to support the affected New York City neighborhood.

cards.headline: Backrooms Director Says AI Use Defeats the Purpose of Filmmaking
cards.teaser: Kane Parsons told an Australian outlet he gets no enjoyment from generative AI tools.
cards.body:
Kane Parsons, the 20-year-old filmmaker behind the Backrooms series, opposes the use of artificial intelligence in filmmaking. In an interview with The Australian, Parsons explained that generative AI provides him no creative satisfaction and undermines the core purpose of making films.

Parsons said he shares the views of most well-adjusted people who reject AI's dominance in Hollywood. He expressed a desire for the technology to be removed from the filmmaking industry entirely.

cards.headline: Pace Gallery Cuts 50 Artists and 50 Staff Members
cards.teaser: The major art gallery reduced both its roster and workforce.
cards.body:
Pace Gallery announced it is dropping 50 artists from its representation roster and eliminating 50 staff positions, representing a significant contraction for one of the art world's largest commercial operations. The New York Times reported the reductions but did not specify which artists or positions were affected.

The gallery has not publicly explained the reasons behind the cuts.

cards.headline: Doja Cat Criticizes Elon Musk While Requesting Platform Changes
cards.teaser: The Grammy winner asked the platform owner to restore audio posts while insulting him.
cards.body:
Doja Cat posted on X requesting that Elon Musk reinstate the audio post feature on the platform. In the same message, she insulted the billionaire owner with profane language and unflattering physical descriptions, calling him a barrel chested ewok and saying he looks like he eats sand.

The musician's approach of combining a feature request with personal attacks makes it unlikely she will receive a favorable response. Musk owns and operates the social media platform formerly known as Twitter.

cards.headline: Love Island USA Contestant Apologizes After Expulsion for Using Racial Slur
cards.teaser: Vasana Montgomery was removed from the show after old social media videos surfaced.
cards.body:
Vasana Montgomery, a 25-year-old from Beaverton, Oregon, was expelled from Love Island USA Season 8 after videos surfaced of her using the N-word in social media posts from her teenage years. She had been cast in the show before the removal.

Montgomery issued a public apology on Wednesday, acknowledging the videos and stating there is no excuse for her language.

cards.headline: Jessica Simpson Discusses Sobriety During California Concert
cards.teaser: The singer reflected on her alcohol abuse during a performance.
cards.body:
Jessica Simpson spoke about her sobriety during a concert in California. The singer took time during her performance to discuss her past struggles with alcohol, describing drinking as a crutch that was not working for her.

Simpson has previously been public about her journey to sobriety. She used the concert appearance to share her reflections on overcoming alcohol abuse with the audience.

hero.headline: Trump to nominate Todd Blanche as attorney general
hero.body:
President Trump announced at a White House dinner that he will nominate Todd Blanche to serve as attorney general. A video of the event was posted on social media by a White House aide, capturing Trump's statement that he plans to formally nominate Blanche.

Blanche, who has served as one of Trump's personal attorneys, would lead the Department of Justice if confirmed by the Senate. The attorney general oversees federal law enforcement, including the FBI, and directs the department's legal positions on behalf of the executive branch. The role has remained one of the most politically sensitive positions in the cabinet.

The announcement comes as Trump continues to shape his administration with loyalists in key positions. Blanche represented Trump in several high-profile legal matters before the president returned to office. His nomination will require Senate confirmation, where Republicans hold a majority but must still navigate the confirmation process.

The choice of Blanche signals Trump's continued preference for advisers with whom he has personal relationships and trust. The attorney general position has seen significant turnover during Trump's political career, with past occupants facing pressure over the independence of the Justice Department versus loyalty to the president.

However, Blanche faces immediate scrutiny over his handling of the Epstein Files Transparency Act. An investigative journalist and legal analyst filed a lawsuit in Washington DC federal court accusing Blanche of a "brazen, shocking, and ongoing violation" of the law requiring the Justice Department to release all documents related to Jeffrey Epstein. Congress passed the transparency act in November with a December 19, 2025 deadline for full document release.

The lawsuit alleges that Blanche, who served as deputy attorney general, has delayed the process and released only a fraction of available documents. It accuses him of missing statutory deadlines for document production, making improper redactions, failing to explain redactions as required by law, and withholding documents after release.

Blanche has argued that redactions were necessary to protect the identities of Epstein's victims, many of them minors, and acknowledged that "mistakes are inevitable." However, critics have questioned the department's process for determining which papers to withhold and which redactions to make. Some victims have complained that their sensitive personal information was improperly exposed in releases.

The Justice Department's office of the inspector general launched an audit into the department's compliance with the Epstein Files Transparency Act last week.

If confirmed, Blanche would take over the Justice Department at a time when it faces questions about prosecutorial priorities and its relationship with the White House. The formal nomination is expected to be submitted to the Senate in the coming days, beginning what could be a contentious confirmation battle where his record on transparency and document release will likely come under intense examination.

cards.headline: Democrats demand explanation for reported White House role in Trump Jr. loan
cards.teaser: Democratic lawmakers are seeking answers after reports that a White House official intervened to secure a Pentagon loan for a company linked to the president's son.
cards.body:
Several Democratic lawmakers are demanding a full explanation following a report that a White House official intervened to grant a $620 million Pentagon loan to a company linked to President Trump's eldest son. The lawmakers described the reported intervention as what appears to be an egregious example of Trump administration corruption involving the White House delivering benefits to entities connected to the president's family.

The loan approval raises questions about potential conflicts of interest and whether White House influence was used to benefit the Trump family financially. Democrats have requested documentation and details about the decision-making process that led to the Pentagon loan approval.

cards.headline: Hilton and Becerra lead in California governor primary
cards.teaser: Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra are leading early returns in California's primary to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
California's primary election showed Xavier Becerra leading the Democratic race and Steve Hilton ahead among Republicans competing to replace term-limited Governor Gavin Newsom. Democrats Katie Porter and Tom Steyer also ran for their party's nomination, while Chad Bianco challenged Hilton on the GOP side.

The race reflects deeper divisions within California's Democratic Party. While establishment favorite Becerra has followed a traditional, corporate-friendly path, Tom Steyer's campaign offered an alternative vision that some see as potentially reshaping the party's direction. The winner will oversee the world's fourth-largest economy.

cards.headline: Israel and Lebanon agree to full ceasefire contingent on Hezbollah withdrawal
cards.teaser: Israel and Lebanon reached a ceasefire agreement that requires Hezbollah to halt attacks and withdraw operatives from southern Lebanon.
cards.body:
Israel and Lebanon have agreed to implement a full ceasefire to end hostilities, according to a joint statement from the US State Department. The agreement requires Hezbollah to completely halt attacks and withdraw all operatives from southern Lebanon.

The US rejected "any attempt, by any state or non-state actor, to hold Lebanon's future hostage." The ceasefire represents a significant development as the Trump administration seeks to overcome barriers to a broader agreement with Iran, of which Hezbollah is aligned.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Former Biden administration official Deb Haaland secured the Democratic nomination in New Mexico's gubernatorial race.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, a former Biden administration official, won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor. Her primary victory sets up a general election matchup in November.

If elected, Haaland would become the first female Native American governor in U.S. history.

cards.headline: Army identifies soldier killed in Iraq training accident
cards.teaser: The Army named the American soldier who died alongside a British service member during a training incident at an airbase in Iraq.
cards.body:
The Army identified Sgt. Devin A. Seibel, 26, of Robinson, Texas, as the American soldier who died on May 31 at Erbil Airbase in what the Pentagon called a training-related incident. The announcement came in a statement released late Wednesday.

Seibel died alongside a British Army soldier during the military training accident in Iraq. The Pentagon has described the incident as training-related but has not provided additional details about the circumstances surrounding the deaths.

cards.headline: House rebukes Max Miller for Hezbollah accusation against Rashida Tlaib
cards.teaser: The Ohio Republican's remarks accusing Representative Rashida Tlaib of associating with Hezbollah were stricken from the congressional record.
cards.body:
Representative Max Miller had his remarks stricken from the House record after accusing Representative Rashida Tlaib of associating with Hezbollah. During debate on a Lebanon war powers resolution, Miller said of Tlaib that Hezbollah is a terrorist organization and its members are butchers that you like to hang out with to a certain extent.

The rebuke came as tensions in the House boiled over during debate on Tlaib's push to pass a resolution constraining Trump's actions on Lebanon. The fight has sparked divisions among Democrats and led to an explosive cross-partisan exchange that briefly halted House proceedings.
